steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Ugh, what a stench.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: All these years and they still won't make better camouflage cream—it wouldn't do any harm for us to at least smell different from the Seaborn, you know.

spans.text: All these years and they still won't make better camouflage cream—it wouldn't do any harm for us to at least
different from the Seaborn, you know.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Don't move so much, Shark. It'll only make the smell stronger.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: When you smell this much like a Seaborn, I might hack at you on instinct.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: The whole plateau is trembling... Those giant wormlike Seaborn are tunneling through the rock beneath us.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Stay concealed.

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: (Vacuole lightly trembles)

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: (Core shudders fiercely)

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Look at those numbers. Honestly, between the currents and the Seaborn, who's carrying who?

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: They're flooding towards the frontline. I can't imagine...

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Can't imagine what the soldiers there are fighting through.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Snap out of it, Skadi. You'll crush your hilt doing that.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: We mourn those on the front best by completing our mission.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Thanks to the Legions' fleets containing the Seaborn swarm, we were able to slip in and plant this beacon deep in the nest.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Even a single plant could alert the Seaborn to us, if it happens to be assimilated. There is no room for negligence on our path forward.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: The great bleached coral will cover us as we dive for the depths of the rift.

steps.name: Specter & Skadi
steps.text: Yes, Captain.

steps.name: Beacon Tower Technician
steps.text: Jordi, right? Fast learner.

steps.name: Beacon Tower Technician
steps.text: A lot of students come here on work experience. With all the operation protocol, it never takes more than a day for them to slip up. You, though, picked it up just by watching for a little while.

steps.name: Beacon Tower Technician
steps.text: You done this before?

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Just a bit. I've done some work in an Iberian lighthouse. The beacons share a few principles with it, here and there.

steps.name: Beacon Tower Technician
steps.text: I see, so you're into engineering. Explains a lot.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: I've worked longest as a caregiver, though.

steps.name: Beacon Tower Technician
steps.text: 'Caregiver'? What kind of job's that?

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Ah, er, watching over the sick and elderly, taking care of their daily needs... Sorting out all the little things for them.

steps.name: Beacon Tower Technician
steps.text: Gotcha. So it's like slapping Little Handy modules 153 and 274 in at the same time.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Um, but the Little Handy is impersonal... right?

steps.name: Beacon Tower Technician
steps.text: That's correct.

steps.name: Beacon Tower Technician
steps.text: You look taut as a wire, Jordi. This isn't an exam on Ægir general knowledge.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: I just want to ask... if the Little Handy has no personality, how is it supposed to meet the emotional needs of its patients?

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: To care for people is to meet them in their weakest, most vulnerable moments, after all.

steps.name: Beacon Tower Technician
steps.text: I'd say physical frailty doesn't particularly inspire emotional needs in us. And if we're headed for the grave, even with illness, we don't feel especially vulnerable, either.

steps.name: Beacon Tower Technician
steps.text: We do let the old and sick request some final company before their euthanasia, though. Usually a leading philosopher will come in. Scholars from whatever field in general, really.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: I-I know nothing about philosophy...

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: I just talk to them about the most banal things. Food, flowers, sunshine, and so on. But for some reason, they're always so happy to listen.

steps.name: Beacon Tower Technician
steps.text: You're a great guy, Jordi.

steps.name: Beacon Tower Technician
steps.text: That shows how keen you are at grasping people's moods. No promises, but something tells me you'd shine in the Institute of Development Planning or Institute of Incubation too.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: C-Could I?

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: ...Regardless, thank you so much! I've finished resetting the storage facilities here!

steps.name: Beacon Tower Technician
steps.text: Wonderful work. Now, about—

steps.name: Beacon Tower Technician
steps.text: Wait. Did you just see something zip past the hologram?

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Wha—

steps.name: Beacon Tower Technician
steps.text: INTRUDER—

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: You?

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: Young man, you saw none of this. You have no reason to complicate things.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Wait!

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Shark's saw will be too loud. Skadi, you open the way.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Cut through this cluster, as quietly as you can.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Alright.
For but an instant, the invading Hunters are bathed in vivid color and indistinct light.
That which the Iberians call nethersea brand creeps across the coral layers, the spawn of the many lilting in their craggy nests.
Eggs are swept from this cliff face as the currents pass, metamorphosing as they spiral down, indescribable folds yet unfolding, until a Seaborn form emerges.

steps.name: Nascent Seaborn
steps.text: (Soft membrane stirs)

steps.name: Nascent Seaborn
steps.text: (Creased skin shudders)
The newborns silently gather together, their trembling bodies echoing all throughout the nest. Intertwining palps and feelers, they sweep each other off for far away.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: They just keep on leaving the nest. Rushing... for the frontline.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Wait, don't you think something's off? How did that one turn into a whole bunch out of nowhere?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: What is it doing? Multiplying? Splitting?

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: I've had this gnawing feeling ever since we bailed out the fleet. Swordfish, have these assholes evolved even more?

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: The Seaborn are forever evolving.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Skadi, can you remember the first Seaborn you ever killed?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Not really. Just that it had a lot of gross tentacles.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: That's what I mean. Tentacles, stingers, chitinous shells... We could still discern the organs, identify their functions at a glance.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Prior to this, the Seaborn's only skill was to hijack whatever evolutionary progress other species had accrued over the epochs.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: But now we've got these things...

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: I can't begin to tell what their organs are. If I didn't know better, I might not even think to connect them to the fodder we were slaughtering just three months ago.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: ...The Seaborn's needs have outgrown the evolutionary advancements. They've begun seeking their own answers.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Which means their evolutionary course now transcends our knowledge.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: If we are unable to gloss their physical composition, unable to discern their organs' unique functions, unable to predict the direction they will evolve...

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: We won't know how to kill them.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: We could fetch a specimen for Advisor Blandus, while we evacuate.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Still, the mission takes priority for now.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Skadi, you and I will find where the wall hasn't yet been branded, embed the beacon there, and activate it.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Laurentina, spot our surroundings. We withdraw as soon as it's planted, without delay.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: Greetings, Doctor of Rhodes Island, and well met in Milliarium. At long last, our first official conversation.

options: Well, Kal'tsit's the official Iberian envoy.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: Save your modesty. Dr. Kal'tsit's awe-inspiring knowledge transcends the boundaries of space and time.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: So for her to be keeping you up her sleeve, the depths you hide must be deeper still.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: Whether you come to me in doubt, or with conclusions of your own to share, I am prepared to listen.

options: You sent the Hunters into a literal nest of danger.
You're endangering three of our operators.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: Much like Dr. Kal'tsit, you have misgivings about this decision.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: Yet I had no choice but to order them to meet death in the eye once more; my hand was forced. Only they can break our present impasse.

options: Rational. Maybe a little too rational?

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: The Legions are deployed to capacity. The Abyssal Hunters must assume combat duties, even having recently returned to Ægir. You suspect this situation was deliberately engineered.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: I gather you return from the city with findings of your own.

options: The beacon-weapon link was tampered with.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: Little Handy, priority order. Contact the supervisors for the beacon and Class IV weapons R&D.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: And notify all Legion commanders: leave enough of your fleets at the front to curb the Seaborn and assist the Hunters. The rest should withdraw in order and return to the city. The Sea Patrol will seize the beacon tower right away.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: You have our gratitude for informing us, Doctor.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: I know I owe the two of you an explanation for how I have deployed the Abyssal Hunters.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: We don't hold you accountable on a tactical level. You know their prowess against the Seaborn better than us.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I can only say this. Your powers of observation would not have missed the scales on Gladiia's neck.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: We can assume the Hunters will have no trouble seeing this assignment through, but what was your guarantee they would be spared from mutating while in the nest?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: The word of Advisor Blandus, and nothing more?

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: Advisor Blandus's statement at the tribunal served to strengthen Milliarium's confidence in the Abyssal Hunters.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: I confess, though, it failed to even ease my mind.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I take it the Hunters still weigh heavily on your thoughts.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: ...Ægir never truly wound down the Abyssal Hunter project, following the strike on the Firstborn.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: I've not been involved, but my countrymen have every right to interrogate me for my awareness of it alone.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: For a short time after the Firstborn died, the project went through major upheavals. Anomalies plagued the experiments, and the Church grew only more fixated on the Hunters.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: This suggests there are urgent, hidden truths about the Hunters yet to be found. Yet it also proves that the project can no longer run publicly.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: To this day, it still operates in secret. But even now, Ægir has only three Hunters including Gladiia... No, four.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: For how constantly we iterate on our technology, we have never succeeded in making another Abyssal Hunter.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: No matter how stable the subjects' signs and psychological indicators are, they lose their reason the moment they awaken, immediately corrupting into Seaborn.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: They don't even make it out of the chamber, let alone to the ocean proper.

options: 'Abyssal Hunters are bound by blood.' We forgot...
What IS this blood binding them?

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: We don't know.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: We still don't know why Gladiia's group have kept their reason intact.

options: Sounds like they're your key to solving this.
Yet you chose to send them to the front.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: ...Indeed. For Gladiia, Laurentina, Skadi, and all the participants, it was an irresponsible act.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: But the front lies at Milliarium now.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: We made it in time to cut off the Seaborn tide as it laps at dry land, but Milliarium is far from impregnable. If we fail to open the Waterway now, it is only a matter of time before the city is lost.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: The Seaborn have organized to seize that Waterway by the throat. Storming them head-on will invite a large-scale counterattack.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: At which point, I fear none will survive.

options: Is risking the Hunters a necessary cost here?

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: The Hunters may well give their lives. They may well transform. But right now, they are our greatest hope.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Gladiia has always been skeptical of the Waterway Program's feasibility. It was for that exact reason that she did not hesitate to serve as a link in its chain.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Your doubts and struggles may differ, but all roads lead to the same place in the end. That seems to be an unspoken yet shared understanding among the Ægir.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: ...One not without its sorrows.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: Upon the bricks of the Sophontheatrum entrance, the architect Mártus left this maxim: 'There is no justice here, only the path ahead.'

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: In later generations, some criticized Mártus as being overly fixated on material value, squandering his energy on comparing worth against worth.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: But ultimately, all that mattered to him was Ægir's path forward. Justice was merely a value cherished by the masses; and he preferred to apply his thought elsewhere.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: Perhaps Gladiia and I have been acting on his philosophy without realizing it.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: Dr. Kal'tsit, everything you have said rings all too true. I am bound in the end to carry 'Ægir's arrogance' with me, and nothing will change that.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I would like to amend that wording. 'Arrogance' as a word seems insufficient to describe Ægir.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: You respect equally the humanity of your every citizen. To realize each individual's worth is the guiding star for your entire society's development.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Yet at the same time, you are capable of making the cruelest judgments, and calmly accepting them, for the sake of Ægir's survival as a whole.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: 'Calmly'... you say?

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: We Ægir are not cold-blooded. Whenever you would feel wrath, our own hearts are far from unstirring.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: These are feelings I had wished to convey to Gladiia, once upon a time, but I realized I had no right to.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: Every decision I made for her, I based in pure rationality. How natural, then, that I lost that right. How dare I ask for an emotional pardon.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: The same is true, even now.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: And so, 'calmly,' I accept my own judgment.

steps.name: 'Little Handy'
steps.text: The designated individual has been contacted. Advisor Blandus did not pick up.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: Dr. Kal'tsit, Doctor. I am deeply sorry I could not give you an appropriate answer.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: But right now, I ask that you permit me to carry out my duty.
